survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Kosovo using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting typically relies on sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates and correct standard errors. The factsheet itself does not specify the exact weight variable name(s) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the precise implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported means, shares at proficiency levels, and trend comparisons should be treated as survey-weighted estimates with uncertainty intervals, even though the weight variable names are not shown in this excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive results factsheet rather than an empirical student-level modeling study that specifies how plausible values (PVs) and missing data were handled in estimation. PISA achievement reporting in factsheets is based on OECD’s standard scaling and reporting procedures, but the excerpt does not provide the PV combination rule or the missing-data treatment used in the underlying database production. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported at the level of methodological detail required for extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2022 analytic sample for Kosovo that completed the assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, reported as 6,027 students in 229 schools (about 86% of the total population of 15-year-olds). The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond the standard PISA participation/quality standards; it states that in Kosovo all data met PISA quality standards and were fit for reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Kosovo performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2015 and 2018). It reports mean performance trends, shares of students below/at proficiency baselines (e.g., Level 2), and the distribution of top performers (Level 5 or 6) across subjects, with uncertainty indicated via confidence intervals. The factsheet also highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles and top/bottom quarters), gender differences, and selected student and school experiences (belonging, discipline, safety, bullying, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences). It notes that Kosovo met PISA sampling/quality standards for 2022, and that an asterisk in other countries would indicate caution due to unmet sampling standards. No student-level predictive modeling or ML estimation is conducted in this factsheet; it is descriptive reporting based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database.
